JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a classic case of a high-quality franchise that has been re-rated far beyond what its fundamentals support. The stock trades at 25.9x P/E (top of 16.3-26.8x range, up from 17.3x a year ago) while normalized earnings power is roughly flat (~$8.60-$9.16 annualized from $2.12-$2.29 quarterly EPS excluding the Q1 2025 one-time gain). ROE has actually declined from 0.279 to 0.259 over the same period, meaning the multiple expansion is not justified by improving returns. The earnings yield of 3.9% now sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.41%, eliminating the defensive premium rationale. Q4 operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% QoQ to $2.51B, and net margin dropped from 0.273 to 0.218 (a 5.5pp decline driven by the Q1 2025 outlier rolling off TTM). While the qualitative franchise is strong (75%+ #1/#2 market share, AAA credit, raised FY2026 guidance to $100.3-$101.3B, Ottava milestone), these positives are already reflected in the 47% 52-week rally and peak-valuation pricing. The talc litigation (67,000 lawsuits, $6.5B settlement plan, failed bankruptcy strategy) adds unquantified tail risk. At this valuation, any further earnings disappointment or litigation development could trigger a significant de-rating. The combination of stretched valuation, margin compression, deteriorating cash flow, and below-Treasury earnings yield makes JNJ fundamentally unattractive at current levels.
